milestones.title: Phase 2: Single-machine deployment
milestones.description: Deploy a web app with a database from scratch, 2–3 weeks

milestones.title: Phase 3: Cluster & failures
milestones.description: Small k8s cluster, DB replication, load testing, 3–4 weeks

milestones.title: Phase 4: Choose a direction
milestones.description: Pick a direction, do course labs, read papers

issues.title: [P1-0] Spin up a cloud VM as the practice environment
issues.body:
Do this on day one. Every Phase 1 exercise happens on this machine, so you get used to the cloud console along the way.

## Tasks
- [ ] Sign up for AWS or GCP; launch a free-tier Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 VM (smallest size is fine)
- [ ] Generate an ssh key pair and log in with it (disable password login)
- [ ] Security group: open only port 22; open others as needed later
- [ ] Set a billing alert so the free tier running out doesn't cost you
- [ ] Create a non-root daily user with sudo

## Log
Write in `notes/`: what a security group is, why the box wasn't reachable at first, what the public vs private IP are.

issues.title: [P1-1] Linux command line
issues.body:
About 1 week, an hour a day. Full checklist in `docs/phase-1.md` §1.

## What to know
- [ ] File ops `ls cd cp mv rm mkdir find cat less head tail`
- [ ] Permissions `chmod chown sudo`, rwx / 755
- [ ] Processes `ps top htop kill`, PIDs, signals, background jobs
- [ ] Text `grep sed awk`, pipes, redirection `> >> 2>&1`
- [ ] Network tools `ssh scp curl wget ping ss dig`
- [ ] `systemctl` / `journalctl` / `/var/log`
- [ ] Env vars, `PATH`, `.bashrc`, symlinks
- [ ] `apt`
- [ ] A shell script under 20 lines with a loop and a conditional

## Resources
- MIT Missing Semester, first few lectures
- linuxjourney.com
- OverTheWire Bandit

## Self-test (close this issue only when all pass)
- [ ] Without looking anything up, ssh into a remote box, find the top-CPU process and kill it
- [ ] From a huge log, extract lines containing "error" and count them per hour
- [ ] Script: walk a directory, compress every .log older than 7 days

issues.title: [P1-2] Networking basics
issues.body:
About 1 week. Goal: be able to picture everything from "type a URL" to "page renders". Full checklist in `docs/phase-1.md` §2.

## What to know
- [ ] Layering
- [ ] DNS: A / CNAME, why changes take time
- [ ] IPs and ports, public vs private, 80 and 443
- [ ] TCP vs UDP, three-way handshake
- [ ] HTTP/HTTPS: methods, status codes, headers, cookies, certificate chain
- [ ] NAT, firewalls, security groups
- [ ] Load balancers and reverse proxies
- [ ] `ping traceroute dig curl -v telnet`

## Resources
- Kurose & Ross ch. 1–2 (skim), Julia Evans' networking zines
- Hands-on: `curl -v` a site and understand every line; `dig` a domain

## Self-test
- [ ] Explain in your own words everything from typing github.com to the page appearing
- [ ] A service on the VM isn't reachable — list at least 4 causes and how to rule each out
- [ ] 502 vs 504: know which layer broke

issues.title: [P1-3] Operating systems basics
issues.body:
About 1 week. If you've taken an OS course, skip straight to the self-test. Full checklist in `docs/phase-1.md` §3.

## What to know
- [ ] Processes vs threads
- [ ] Virtual memory, OOM
- [ ] CPU scheduling, time slices
- [ ] File descriptors, inodes
- [ ] System calls, user vs kernel mode
- [ ] Locks, deadlock, race conditions
- [ ] `/proc`, `ulimit`
- [ ] **cgroups and namespaces** (the basis of containers — must understand)

## Resources
- OSTEP: Virtualization part + first few Concurrency chapters (~150 pages)
- `strace` a program; `cat /proc/<pid>/status`

## Self-test
- [ ] Explain why a program can use 8 GB on a 4 GB machine
- [ ] One sentence: the real difference between a container and a VM
- [ ] Seeing OOM killed, know what happened and where the logs are

issues.title: [P1-4] Docker
issues.body:
3–5 days. Last on purpose — it's the other three applied. Full checklist in `docs/phase-1.md` §4.

## What to know
- [ ] Image vs container
- [ ] Dockerfile: `FROM RUN COPY WORKDIR EXPOSE CMD`, layers and caching
- [ ] `build run ps logs exec stop rm`, `-p -v -e`
- [ ] Docker Compose
- [ ] What a volume is and why data vanishes without one
- [ ] Docker Hub push / pull

## Resources
- Docker's Get Started guide
- Containerize any small project you've written

## Self-test
- [ ] Dockerfile for a project with a reasonable image size
- [ ] Compose: web app + PostgreSQL, app connects, data survives restart
- [ ] A container won't start — debug with `docker logs` / `docker exec`

issues.title: [P2-1] Write a minimal CRUD app and containerize it
issues.body:
Code in `projects/phase-2/`.

- [ ] Any language (Flask / Express / Go): a CRUD app backed by PostgreSQL
- [ ] Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml
- [ ] `docker compose up` works locally
- [ ] Add a `/health` endpoint — monitoring and k8s will both need it

issues.title: [P2-2] Deploy by hand to the cloud VM with a domain and HTTPS
issues.body:
- [ ] Install Docker on the Phase 1 VM (or a fresh one) and run the app
- [ ] Security group: open 80 / 443
- [ ] Get a domain, add an A record pointing at the server
- [ ] HTTPS with Caddy (easiest) or Nginx + certbot
- [ ] https://your-domain loads in a browser

## Log
How is the certificate issued? How does Let's Encrypt verify you own the domain? What happens when it expires? Write it in `notes/questions.md`.

issues.title: [P2-3] Auto-deploy with GitHub Actions
issues.body:
- [ ] Workflow: push to main → build image → push to a registry (GHCR is free)
- [ ] Server pulls the new image and restarts (ssh script, or watchtower)
- [ ] Secrets (ssh key, registry token) go in GitHub Secrets, never in code
- [ ] Push a deliberately broken version; see what happens; think about rollback

## Log
Why does Actions sometimes queue? Where do runners come from? How are secrets injected into the build without leaking?

issues.title: [P2-4] Add monitoring: Prometheus + Grafana + logs
issues.body:
- [ ] App exposes `/metrics` (request count, latency histogram)
- [ ] Prometheus scrapes it; Grafana dashboard: QPS, p50/p99 latency, error rate
- [ ] Central logs: Grafana Cloud free tier or local Loki
- [ ] One alert: service down / error rate over threshold → notify you

## Log
One machine's logs are findable. What about a thousand? That's the observability field.

issues.title: [P2-5] Phase 2 retro: organize the "why?" log
issues.body:
Phase 2 done when:
- [ ] Public domain over HTTPS
- [ ] Push to main is live within 5 minutes
- [ ] Grafana shows request rate and latency
- [ ] At least 10 entries in `notes/questions.md`

Retro:
- [ ] Group the questions by layer (storage / scheduling / network / security / observability)
- [ ] Which group do you most want to chase? Write a paragraph
- [ ] If in school: you now have something to show — go talk to a systems professor

issues.title: [P3-1] Stand up a Kubernetes cluster and run 3 replicas
issues.body:
Code in `projects/phase-3/`.

- [ ] Local cluster with kind or k3s (or a managed k8s free tier)
- [ ] Deployment / Service / Ingress; Phase 2 app with 3 replicas
- [ ] Liveness / readiness probes using `/health`
- [ ] Resource requests / limits
- [ ] `kubectl delete pod` one replica; watch traffic shift and recovery time

## Log
Why did the scheduler put the pod on that node? What happens when limits are too low?

issues.title: [P3-2] PostgreSQL primary/replica, then kill the primary
issues.body:
- [ ] Set up PostgreSQL streaming replication: one primary, one replica
- [ ] Verify writes to the primary show up on the replica
- [ ] Kill the primary. What happens to the app? Does the replica promote itself? (Probably not)
- [ ] Manually promote the replica and point the app at it
- [ ] Read how Patroni does automatic failover

## Log
This is the "who becomes the new primary" leader-election problem. Why can't both be primary? Come back to this when you read the Raft paper.

issues.title: [P3-3] Load test, find the bottleneck, tune
issues.body:
- [ ] k6 or locust; ramp up until errors or latency spike
- [ ] Check Grafana: is the bottleneck app CPU? DB connections? Network?
- [ ] Try at least two optimizations (more replicas / connection pool / cache / adjust limits) and compare before/after
- [ ] Write a load-test report: QPS, p50/p99, bottleneck, changes, conclusion

## Self-test
If traffic goes up 10×, what breaks first?

issues.title: [P3-4] Phase 3 retro: are you hooked on keeping systems up?
issues.body:
Phase 3 done when:
- [ ] 3 replicas; killing any one doesn't interrupt service
- [ ] Did a primary → replica failover at least once
- [ ] A load-test report exists

Honest answers:
- [ ] Which moments this month were exciting? Which were "just get the config done"?
- [ ] Are you hooked on making the system stable, or does it feel like tedious configuration?
- [ ] Both answers are useful. Write them in `notes/phase-3-retro.md`, then go to `docs/phase-4.md` and pick a direction

issues.title: [P4] Pick a direction and do the core labs of one systems course
issues.body:
Use the table in `docs/phase-4.md`.

- [ ] Write `notes/why-this-direction.md`: why this one, which moments in Phases 2–3 pointed at it
- [ ] Pick the matching course (6.824 / 15-445 / CS162 / CS144) and do its core labs
- [ ] Read 5 papers in the direction, one page of notes each in `notes/papers/`
- [ ] If in school: take the Phase 2/3 work to a professor in that area and talk
- [ ] Open new issues to track lab progress

issues.title: [Reading] One classic paper a week
issues.body:
Starting in Phase 1, one paper a week; list in `docs/reading-list.md`. For each, write a page in `notes/papers/`: the problem, the core idea, what you didn't get.

## Starter
- [ ] MapReduce (OSDI 2004)
- [ ] GFS (SOSP 2003)
- [ ] Dynamo (SOSP 2007)
- [ ] Raft (ATC 2014)

## Intermediate
- [ ] Borg (EuroSys 2015)
- [ ] Spanner (OSDI 2012)
- [ ] Firecracker (NSDI 2020)
- [ ] Dapper (2010)

This issue spans all phases and stays open.
